site.tagline: Simple on the surface. Powerful underneath.
site.description: Loupe is a free, open-source mail app for Android: as calm as the best phone mail apps, with desktop-grade search, rules and encryption. No tracking, no servers.

common.theme: Switch between light and dark theme
common.appEnglish: The Loupe app is in English for now; more languages will follow.

footer.about: A calm mail app with serious tools underneath. Free, open source, and private by design.
footer.copyright_html: © {year} {owner} and contributors. Loupe is open source under the {licence}.
footer.independent: Loupe is an independent project. It is not affiliated with Mozilla, Thunderbird, Apple, Google or Microsoft; their names are used only to describe compatibility.

home.title: Loupe
home.lead: Loupe is a calm, fast mail app with desktop-class tools underneath: expression search, server-side rules, OpenPGP and S/MIME. It talks to your mail server and nobody else.
home.fact1: No account, no ads, no tracking
home.lensHint: Find exactly what you're looking for
home.pillarsTitle: Simple on the surface. Powerful underneath.
home.pillarsLead: The everyday stays quiet: read, reply, archive. The moment you need more, it's there, without a settings maze.
home.calmText: A clean list, readable messages and gestures you already know. No feeds, no badges begging for attention.
home.sharpText: Expression search, Smart Mailboxes, Sieve rules, tags and keyboard shortcuts, the tools power users miss on mobile.
home.privateText: No Loupe servers in the middle. An encrypted store on the phone, remote images off, trackers unwrapped.
home.searchLead: Pull down and type. Loupe understands fields, groups, dates and negation, shows results from the phone instantly, and streams in the rest from your server.
home.searchMore_html: Save any search as a Smart Mailbox. It's stored on your own mail server, so it shows up on your other devices too, or make it a rule.
home.readingLead: Desktop-sized HTML becomes a clean, legible page. Footers shrink to fine print, photo grids become a carousel, and dark mode fixes the colours that would disappear.
home.readingTick1: Readable, Original and Plain views, one tap apart
home.readingTick3: Patches on mailing lists drawn as coloured diffs
home.featuresTitle: The details you'd expect from a desktop client.
home.privacyTitle: There's no Loupe cloud. That's the point.
home.privacyLead: Your phone talks to your mail server, directly. Loupe has no backend to breach, no analytics to opt out of, and nothing to sell.
home.privacy1Text: Mail goes between your phone and your provider.
home.privacy2Text: No analytics, crash reports or ad identifiers.
home.privacy3Text: An encrypted database for mail and the search index.
home.privacy4Text: Remote images off by default, redirect links unwrapped.
home.providersTitle: Works with the mail you already have
home.providersNote_html: Sign in with Google and Microsoft for Gmail, Outlook.com and Microsoft 365, and import from Thunderbird's “Export for Mobile” QR code. Accounts guide
home.openTitle: Open source, down to the last test.
home.openLead: Every line is public under the {licence}. Nightly builds come straight from GitHub Actions, so what you install is what you can read.
home.finalTitle: Give your inbox a closer look.
home.finalText: Loupe is free. If it earns a place on your phone, pay what you want, and help keep the nightly builds coming.
home.whyTitle: Phone mail apps make you choose.
home.whyLead: The simple ones are lovely until you need a message from two years ago. The powerful ones bury the inbox under toolbars. And many sync your mailbox through servers of their own. Loupe refuses all three trade-offs.
home.compareNote: A comparison with common phone mail apps in general, not with any one app.
home.companionTitle: A companion for your desktop client
home.companionText: Loupe isn't trying to replace the mail client on your computer. It's for people who use Thunderbird or another desktop client and want the same power on the phone: the same tags, the same rules on the same server, and a QR code to bring accounts across.

readable.title: Readable mode
readable.text: HTML mail rebuilt to fit your screen: real text sizes, footers as fine print, photos in a swipeable carousel.

search.title: Expression search
search.text: Chips or typed queries like from:alice and is:unread. Results from the phone appear at once, the server streams in after.

smart.title: Smart Mailboxes that travel
smart.text: Saved searches stored on your own mail server, so they follow you to every device.

rules.title: Rules, on the device or the server
rules.text: Turn any search into a rule. Run it on the phone, or as Sieve on your server so it works while you sleep.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.text: Every newsletter by sender, with read rates and a one-tap unsubscribe centre that runs on your phone.

snooze.title: Snooze that syncs
snooze.text: Snoozed mail lives in a folder on your server, so other clients that follow the convention see it too.

send.title: Undo and schedule send
send.text: Take back a message in the first seconds, or write now and send tomorrow at nine.

encryption.title: OpenPGP and S/MIME
encryption.text: Encrypt and sign with either standard. OpenPGP works with Thunderbird and Autocrypt.

phishing.title: Explainable phishing check
phishing.text: Suspicious links and look-alike domains are flagged, with the reason in plain words.

calendar.title: Calendar invitations
calendar.text: Accept, Maybe or Decline right above the message, with both time zones when they differ.

protocols.title: IMAP and JMAP
protocols.text: Any IMAP provider with autoconfig, plus native JMAP for Fastmail and Stalwart.

tablet.title: Tablets and keyboards
tablet.text: Three panes, keyboard shortcuts, drag and drop, and a command palette on Ctrl+K.

reading.title: Every message, made for a phone.
reading.lead: Most HTML mail is designed for a desktop inbox. Readable mode rebuilds it for the screen in your hand, and the original is one tap away.

p1.title: Readable, Original, Plain
p1.text: Three views per message; Loupe can remember your choice per sender. Plain comes in Sans and Mono.

p2.title: Photos as a gallery
p2.text: Image-heavy mail turns into a carousel; tap for a full-screen gallery.

p3.title: Dark mode that works
p3.text: Colours fixed for dark backgrounds, so dark text never disappears.

p4.title: Footers as fine print
p4.text: Legal blocks and unsubscribe boilerplate shrink out of the way.

search.title: Find anything, the way you think.
search.lead: Pull down to search. Tap chips, or type an expression with the same power as a desktop client. Loupe answers from the phone at once and asks the server in parallel.

p1.title: Chips and expressions
p1.text: Type an expression and each part becomes a chip in plain words; tap one to change it.

p2.title: Local first, server after
p2.text: Instant results from the encrypted on-device index, then the rest of your archive.

p3.title: Smart Mailboxes
p3.text: Save a search. It is stored on your server and appears on your other devices.

p4.title: Search to rule
p4.text: Any search can become a device or server rule in two taps.

organising.title: Inbox zero without the busywork.
organising.lead: Swipes with Undo, a Filter button for the views you use every day, tags that match Thunderbird, and snooze that keeps working on your other clients.

p1.title: Swipes with Undo
p1.text: Archive, flag, read or move with a swipe; nothing is final until you say so.

p2.title: Filter button
p2.text: Unread, flagged, with attachments, unreplied or addressed to you.

p3.title: Tags
p3.text: Compatible with Thunderbird, so they look the same on your desktop.

p4.title: Snooze
p4.text: Stored on the server as a folder and a keyword, not in a vendor cloud.

subscriptions.title: Newsletters, sorted by the people who send them.
subscriptions.lead: Loupe groups bulk mail by sender, shows how much of it you actually read, and unsubscribes on your phone, without a third-party service reading your inbox.

p1.title: Newsletters and Discussions
p1.text: Bulk senders and the mailing lists you write to, in two tabs.

p2.title: Unsubscribe centre
p2.text: One-click, by mail or on the sender's page: whatever the sender supports.

p3.title: Lists as forums
p3.text: Mailing-list threads read like a forum, with muting per thread.

p4.title: Patches as diffs
p4.text: Patches sent to a list are drawn as coloured diffs, for people who review code by mail.

security.title: No servers. No tracking. No exceptions.
security.lead: Loupe talks to your mail provider and nobody else. There is no Loupe account, no analytics and no crash reporter. Your mail is encrypted on the phone.

p1.title: Encrypted local store
p1.text: Messages and the search index sit in an encrypted database.

p2.title: Remote images blocked
p2.text: Tracking pixels stay silent until you choose to load images.

p3.title: Tracking links unwrapped
p3.text: Redirect wrappers are removed, so you see and visit the real address.

p4.title: OpenPGP and S/MIME
p4.text: Keys on your device, Autocrypt for easy OpenPGP, Android KeyChain certificates for S/MIME.

writing.title: Send with confidence.
writing.lead: Identities and aliases, drafts that save themselves, a few seconds to take a message back, and an Outbox for mail that should go out later.

p1.title: Identities and aliases
p1.text: Reply from the address the mail was sent to, including catch-all aliases.

p2.title: Undo send
p2.text: A short window to change your mind.

p3.title: Scheduled send
p3.text: Pick a time; the Outbox keeps it until then, even offline.

p4.title: Notifications with actions
p4.text: Archive, Mark as Read or Reply from the notification.

features.title: Features
features.description: Readable mode, expression search, Smart Mailboxes, Sieve rules, unsubscribe centre, snooze, OpenPGP and S/MIME: everything Loupe does for your mail.
features.h1_html:
Quiet by default.
Capable when you need it.
features.lead: A tour of what Loupe does today. Everything here is in the current Nightly build, and nothing needs an account with us.
features.principleTitle: Simple by default, powerful on demand.
features.principleLead: Every screen should feel familiar the first time you see it. No power feature gets a permanent button on the main screens; they live in four places instead.
features.place1Text: On messages, senders, chips and folders.
features.place2Text: View Source, every header, and search from this message.
features.place3Text: Everything the chips can do, and more, by typing.
features.place4Text: Server details, sync and the rarely needed switches.
features.rpLead: Every message goes through the same six steps, in the background, with limits on size, depth and time so a hostile message can't stall the app.
features.rp1Text: Broken markup is recovered the way browsers recover it.
features.rp2Text: Scripts, styles, forms, hidden preheaders and spam padding go, and so do tracking pixels.
features.rp3Text: Layout tables become one readable column; real data tables stay tables and scroll on their own.
features.rp4Text: Colours, highlights and emphasis stay; big text becomes a heading, legal footers become fine print.
features.rp5Text: Text that would lose contrast changes lightness but keeps its hue, so a yellow highlight stays yellow.
features.rp6Text: No web view and no JavaScript: nothing in a message can run, and selection and accessibility simply work.
features.seLead: Loupe reads your query once, then asks every place your mail lives in its own language.
features.seLocalText: Full-text search over the encrypted local copy, with results as you type.
features.seImapText: The whole and/or/not tree maps onto the server's own search.
features.seGmailText: Translated into Gmail's own search syntax and run once, across all mail.
features.seJmapText: One nested filter, answered in a single round-trip.
features.seNote: When a server can't express part of a query, Loupe asks for a slightly wider set and filters it on the phone, so the results always match exactly what you typed.
features.jmapTitle: Built around JMAP, fluent in IMAP.
features.jmapLead: Loupe's own data model follows JMAP, the modern mail protocol. IMAP accounts are translated into it, and JMAP accounts speak it natively.
features.jmap1Text: Only what changed since last time crosses the network.
features.jmap2Text: Complex queries answered by the server in a single request.
features.jmap3Text: Mail is submitted through the same connection.
features.jmap4Text: Changes pushed from the server, and rules written over JMAP.
features.sec1: Encrypted connections only: no silent fallback to plain text.
features.sec2: A self-signed certificate is trusted only after you've seen and confirmed its fingerprint.
features.sec3: Messages are taken apart in the background, with limits, so a malformed one can't freeze the app.
features.sec4: Passwords and tokens live in Android's keystore; the mail database is encrypted.

download.title: Download Loupe for Android
download.description: Download Loupe, the free and open-source mail app for Android 7 and later. Pay what you want, or nothing at all. Signed nightly builds from GitHub.
download.lead: Loupe is free and open source. If it's useful to you, pay what you want: it funds development and keeps Loupe independent. No ads and no data sales, ever.
download.why1Text: Development time, an Apple developer account for the iOS version, and test devices.
download.why2Text: Paying unlocks nothing extra. There are no paid tiers and no nag screens in the app.
download.why3Text: Every change to the code becomes a new build. Install updates over the old one; your accounts stay.
download.obtainiumText_html: Add {repo} as an app, and turn on Include prereleases. Obtainium then installs each new Nightly for you.
download.githubText_html: All files of the current build, including the x86_64 APK for emulators. Open the Nightly release
download.buildText_html: Flutter 3.47 and one command. Build from source
download.storesText_html: A Play Store beta and an iOS TestFlight are planned. Follow the blog to hear first.

wall.optional: Paying is optional and unlocks nothing extra: every build is the same free app.
wall.soon: Loupe is free. Donations open soon.

install.step1Text_html: Tap the notification, or find loupe-…-arm64.apk in your Downloads.
install.step2Text_html: Android asks once whether your browser may install apps. Allow it, then tap Install. Later builds install over this one and keep your accounts.
install.step3: Try it, or add your account

install.safety: Every build is made by GitHub Actions from the public source and signed with Loupe's release key. Google Play Protect may still warn about apps from outside the Play Store.

donate.title: Support Loupe

donate.lead: Loupe has no investors, no ads and no data to sell. It is made by one developer, in the open, and funded by the people who use it.

press.title: Press kit
press.description: Logos, app icon, screenshots, brand colours and a fact sheet for writing about Loupe, the free and open-source mail app for Android.
press.lead: Everything you need, free to use in articles, videos and reviews. Questions:
press.sentence: Loupe is a free, open-source mail app for Android that is as simple as the best phone mail apps on the surface, with desktop-class search, rules and encryption underneath.
press.paragraph: Loupe is an independent mail app for Android, with iOS planned. It rebuilds HTML newsletters to fit the phone (Readable mode), searches with a full expression language across the phone and the server, keeps Smart Mailboxes and rules on the user's own mail server, and supports OpenPGP and S/MIME. It works with any IMAP or JMAP provider. Loupe has no servers of its own and collects no data: no analytics, no telemetry, no ads. It is open source under the {licence} and built in public on GitHub.
press.please2: Don't describe Loupe as made by or affiliated with Mozilla or Thunderbird. It's independent; it works with Thunderbird's tags and settings export.
press.please3: Don't change the logo's colours or proportions.
press.logoAlt: Loupe logo: a teal magnifying glass over a white envelope
press.iconAlt: Loupe app icon on its navy tile
press.typeText: Ubuntu, Light for text and Medium for headlines (Ubuntu Font Licence).

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.description: What Loupe has shipped, what's next (Google Play, iOS, verified Google sign-in), what may come later, and what is deliberately not planned.
roadmap.lead: Loupe is built in phases, each with a clear finish line. Here's what's done, what's next, and what is deliberately not on the list.
roadmap.status: Today: used every day on Android, with a new Nightly build after every change. The iOS version is prepared and waits for an Apple developer account.
roadmap.p0Text: The name and licence, the Readable renderer, sync tested against the big providers, the encrypted store and the search parser.
roadmap.p1Text: Accounts with automatic setup, the message list with swipes, Readable, Original and Plain views, search, compose with undo send and an Outbox, notifications and dark mode.
roadmap.p2Text: The full search language, Smart Mailboxes, tags, rules and Sieve, identities, View Source and authentication results, three panes and keyboard shortcuts, scheduled send.
roadmap.p3Text: JMAP accounts for Fastmail and Stalwart: search on the server, sending without SMTP, push from the server, and Sieve over JMAP.
roadmap.p4Text: OpenPGP compatible with Thunderbird, with Autocrypt; S/MIME, including certificates installed on the device.
roadmap.p5Text: Sign in with Google and Microsoft through their verification, a public beta on Google Play, and iOS on TestFlight.
roadmap.p6Text: Only if real needs can't be met by built-in features. See below.
roadmap.later1Text: Fingerprint or PIN before your mail shows.
roadmap.later2Text: A message as an .eml file, a folder as an mbox archive.
roadmap.later3Text: Today the app itself is in English.
roadmap.later4Text: iOS doesn't let apps keep a connection open. An optional relay could send content-free "check now" pushes, but only if it can work without ever seeing mail.
roadmap.notLead: Saying no keeps Loupe small, fast and private. These won't happen, and here's why.
roadmap.not1Text: Loupe keeps mail on the server, so every device sees the same mailbox.
roadmap.not2Text: Microsoft 365 works over IMAP with Microsoft sign-in. Loupe sticks to open standards.
roadmap.not3Text: Their APIs are built around desktop windows, and about half of the popular ones reach into Thunderbird's internals, which a phone app can't offer.
roadmap.not4: A server that holds your password
roadmap.not4Text: Some apps keep your login on their servers to fetch your mail. Loupe never will.
roadmap.not5Text: Loupe is for phones and tablets; your computer already has good mail clients.
roadmap.pluginsText: Most popular desktop add-ons fill gaps that Loupe covers natively: better search, conversations, scheduled send, authentication results, rules. If outside extensions ever become necessary, they'll run in a locked-down sandbox, with permissions you approve and no code downloaded from the internet.
roadmap.howText: Each phase has a finish line, and nothing from the next phase sneaks in early. Bugs come first, then what people ask for in Discussions. Donations buy the time for both.
